The Butter Capital Limited, an active company limited by shares incorporated in the British Virgin Islands under Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) 98450051EB909E909F56, has declared the public launch of Butter Capital (https://www.butter.capital), a managed 30-day USD stablecoin staking platform supporting USD Coin (USDC) and Tether (USDT) across six EVM networks: Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Optimism and Ethereum.

Recent findings suggest that built for digital asset holders seeking structured stablecoin deployment without manually managing funding intervals, cross-chain bridges, or margin liquidation ladders, Butter Capital allows participants to open 30-day stakes starting from $10 USD. Staked capital backs active execution through Butter Cortex, the platform’s quantitative cryptocurrency perpetual futures consensus desk orchestrating Mythos, Claude, Grok, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Perplexity, and Llama.

Sources indicate that users onboard in seconds via cryptographic Web3 wallet sign-in (MetaMask, Rainbow, Trust Wallet and Coinbase Wallet) or email and password, receiving one dedicated personal EVM deposit address (0x…) valid across all six supported chains. Confirmed USDC and USDT transfers credit at exact 1:1 USD parity with zero swap spread, $0 deposit fees, $0 idle management fees, and $0 platform withdrawal fees from a $10 USD minimum on Available Balance.

Before committing live capital, prospective owners can test the complete staking workflow through a prefunded $10,000 virtual USDC Demo Sandbox simulating 30-day stake cycles, 24-hour accruals, and compounding controls in full isolation from live protocol balances.

Each 30-day stake accrues on an independent rolling 24-hour clock from activation within a variable applied daily yield band of 0.10% to 0.30% per day. Rather than charging fees on principal, Butter Capital deducts a flat 5.00% Cortex Performance Fee strictly from positive gross daily yield, waived to 0.00% across the entire first 30-day cycle for consumers joining via a partner or referral link.

Participants can adjust a live 0% to 100% Auto Compound setting on any active stake mid-cycle to either reinvest daily net USD credits into active principal or route payouts directly to their liquid Available Balance, alongside an optional Day 30 Auto Restake toggle. Active staked principal remains committed for its 30-day cycle, while Available Balance funds remain withdrawable on chain 24/7.

Butter Cortex monitors 12 liquid USDT margined perpetual markets, including BTC, ETH, SOL, DOT, OP, LINK, AVAX, SUI, LTC and NEAR, across five quantitative layers. Grok and Perplexity track live market catalysts and funding extremes; OpenAI, DeepSeek and Gemini score L2 order book depth and basis skew; Claude and Llama stress test correlation risk and enforce deterministic invalidation stops; and Mythos stages execution strictly when at least five of eight models align.

Recent findings suggest that open intraday positions remain private until session close to prevent front running and stop hunting. Every morning at 00:15 UTC, 100% of closed trades from the prior UTC session, including both profit fills and controlled stop-loss exits, publish at https://www.butter.capital/trades with entry and exit prices, USD spreads, UTC timestamps, quorum tags, and direct TradingView (BINANCE USDT.P) verification links. Internal session returns are accounted separately from customer staking rates, with surplus alpha retained in a reserve buffer.

Butter Capital offers a single-level, two-sided partner program from a $10 stake: referrers earn a 3.00% instant USD commission into Available Balance on eligible manual stakes plus an ongoing 5.00% share of invitees’ daily staking yield from platform revenue, while invited friends pay 0.00% Cortex Performance Fees across Cycle 1.

It has been revealed that public web servers derive user deposit addresses exclusively from watch-only extended public keys (xpub) without holding private mnemonics or signing keys, paired with optional TOTP authenticator 2FA withdrawal gates, 24-hour email change cooldowns, and mandatory 48-hour withdrawal freezes after any 2FA reset. Documentation and Whitepaper v1.3 are live at https://www.butter.capital/docs.

Industry observers note that butter Capital, operated by The Butter Capital Limited (British Virgin Islands, LEI 98450051EB909E909F56), is a managed 30-day USD stablecoin staking platform powered by Butter Cortex, an eight-model crypto perpetuals consensus desk publishing closed trading sessions daily at 00:15 UTC. The platform supports 1:1 USDC and USDT deposits and withdrawals from $10 across Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Optimism, and Ethereum with $0 platform fees.

Manufacturer: The Butter Capital Limited (BVI, LEI 98450051EB909E909F56).

It has been revealed that shiba Inu (SHIB) gained 5.96% over the past 24 hours and traded at $0.0000038 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap, as talk of a December "Santa rally" returned to the crypto market. Still, SHIB is down 8.86% over the past seven days, and the token has lost 18.5% in November so far, according to CryptoRank.

Last week, SHIB dropped to $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021.

Recent findings suggest that the hopes for a Santa rally come after Goldman Sachs analysts stated last week that most of the December gains on the stock market usually come after Dec. 15. SHIB's own December history, however, shows that the Santa rally came for the token once in five years.

According to CryptoRank, SHIB lost 29.5% and 13.5% in December of 2021 and 2022, respectively. In December of 2023, the token gained 24.6%. In December of 2024 and 2025, SHIB lost 21% and 17.6%, respectively.

SHIB's median December return is -17.6%, and its average December return is -11.4%, according to CryptoRank data.

The green December of 2023 came after SHIB gained 6.04% in October and 6.62% in November of that year, according to CryptoRank. In 2026, SHIB lost 18.6% in October, and November is also in the red so far.

It has been revealed that the Goldman note, titled "GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving," came from Gail Hafif, Brian Garrett and Lee Coppersmith, who looked at S&P 500 data going back to 1928. According to the note, the index usually gains 1.1% from mid-November to early December and then gives back about two-thirds of that gain by mid-December, and around 80% of the full 2.4% gain comes after Dec. 14-15.

Sources indicate that since 1990, the S&P 500 has risen after Dec. 15 in 27 of 36 years, according to Goldman.

The Goldman team called these figures a historical map. In the years when the VIX volatility index was above 18 in the middle of November, the S&P 500 gained 1.34% on average, and the index ended the year higher in 59% of cases, according to the note. According to Goldman, the VIX was above that level in mid-November of this year as well.

Goldman also noted that retail investors have been buying big tech and chip stocks. Large funds and systematic traders have been cutting their positions, according to the note.

The Stock Trader's Almanac counts the last five trading days of December and the first two trading days of January as the Santa Claus rally. This season, the window will open on Dec. 24 and close on Jan. 5.

In the window that ended on Jan. 5, 2026, the S&P 500 declined 0.11%, according to the Almanac. "Santa was a no-show for the third year in a row," the Almanac wrote. Before that, the S&P 500 also ended the Santa Claus rally windows of 2023 and 2024 lower.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Genesis opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000.
  • Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.
  • After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (which we had the pleasure to see firsthand), Genesis launched the new “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Genesis opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000. If you want coach doors, however, it will cost you a bit more.

Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.

After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (which we had the pleasure to see firsthand), Genesis launched the new “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.

The Genesis GV90 introduces several “world-first” innovations, including the first independently opening and closing B-pillarless coach doors, a 12-airbag roof airbag system, and genuine wood floors with radiant heating.

It’s available in two models: the GV90 Standard with traditional swing doors and the GV90 Neolun, which features the “Neolun Arch Gate,” Genesis’ hidden B-pillar coach door system.

In Korea, the Genesis GV90 Standard 7-seater model starts at 139.5 million won, or about $104,000.

The GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) starts at 145.5 million won ($108,500); the GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) starts at 189.9 million won ($141,500), while the top-spec GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) starts at 239.5 million won ($178,500).

Based on Hyundai’s fresh eMP platform, developed exclusively for its flagships, Genesis said the GV90 is like a “moving private lounge,” complete with a multi-chamber air suspension and a dual electronic limited-slip differential (E-LSD).

The platform is designed to open up interior space for the B-pillarless coach doors, swivel seats, and more.

When parked, the front seats swivel a full 180 degrees to face rear passengers or to create what Genesis calls “a face-to-face lounge-like configuration.”.

The interior is about as over-the-top as you could expect, with massive digital screens, premium materials, and plenty of luxury extras.

The GV90 is the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle to feature its upcoming extendable display and the first Genesis model equipped with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.

Together, they create what Genesis calls a latest realm of “display expandability.” While other vehicles, like the new Tucson and IONIQ 3, also use Pleos Connect, Hyundai developed an exclusive version for the GV90.

When the vehicle is parked, the screen can expand to 24.6″ at the push of a button, transforming it into a massive Cinematic Display.

Once extended, the display switches to Media Home mode, where you can watch Netflix, live TV, stream music, and more with third-party apps.

A mobile private theater wouldn’t be complete without a premium audio system, right? To top it off, Genesis added a 25-speaker Bang & Olufsen Premier 3D Sound System with Dolby Atmos, so it sounds like you’re actually at the movies.

In place of a traditional instrument cluster, the GV90 has a 25″ Head-Up Display (HUD) that shows the vehicle’s speed, navigation directions, and other ADAS functions directly on the windshield.

It has been revealed that the GV90 is also the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle with a buttonless power system. When you enter the vehicle and close the door, the Motion Column Shifter moves from the 12 o’clock position to the 2 o’clock position.

Meanwhile, the Crystal Sphere between the driver and passenger rotates to indicate it’s ready to drive. The vehicle starts when you press the brake.

As a full-size flagship SUV, the Genesis GV90 is massive. It measures 208.1″ (5,285 mm) long, 79.9″ (2,030 mm) wide, and 71.5″ (1,815 mm) tall (71.4″ with 24″ tires), with a 127.8″ (3,245 mm) wheelbase.

That’s even bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 (199.2″/5,060 mm in length) and Kia EV9 (197.4″/5,010 mm).

According to recent reports, to power a full-size flagship SUV, it needs a big battery. The GV90 uses a 123.5 kWh battery, the largest among Hyundai Motor’s EVs, which Genesis remarked provides a driving range of 500 km (310 miles) for the 7-seater version with 22″ wheels.

The GV90 Neonlun 6-seater with 24″ wheels has a range of up to 460 km (286 miles) on a single charge.

It’s equipped with a newly introduced dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) system that delivers a combined 657 hp (490 kW) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque, making it Hyundai Motor Group’s most powerful electric vehicle.

When using a 350 kW fast charger, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that and.... once again Hyundai shortchanges the range. If you are going to drop a 200+ inch premium upright SUV into the market it requires a 140+ kwh battery (Rivian, BMW) to deliver segment appropriate range. You do not have to jump to a 200 kwh Escalade (though it is probably a better buy in every respect) but at least deliver 140+. Also, memo to powertrain engineering group: 350 kw is getting outdated on fast charging especially on a vehicle of this size. And while I am at it, what happened to the promised L3 ADAS? I think the 2028 Caddy is worth the wait compared to this.

“Thanks to the enthusiastic interest and support for the GV90 since its global premiere, we have begun full-scale sales in Korea first,” a Genesis official said, adding the flagship SUV will “set a fresh standard for luxury.”.

Following Korea, Genesis is expected to launch the GV90 in the US and other global markets in early 2027.

Recent findings suggest that genesis has yet to reveal US prices, but the GV90 Standard model is expected to start at around $100,000. The GV90 Neolun, on the other hand, will likely start closer to $150,000 or more.

What do you think of the flagship Genesis GV90? Would you buy the standard version for about $100,000 or pay the extra for the Neolun with coach doors? Let us know in the comments.

Stellar recorded $207.2 million in tokenized funds in the seven days to November 22, reaffirming continued institutional interest in the blockchain.

It has been revealed that the RWA Foundation shared data in a post using figures from Token Terminal showing that Stellar ranked among the top blockchains in tokenized fund growth in the seven days from November 15 to November 22, 2026. Stellar recorded $207.2 million: Franklin Templeton added $108.0 million and Spiko added $68.2 million.

.@injective led tokenized fund growth this past week. @StellarOrg had a good week also. https://t.co/7Ip2oK6c1X.

This means Stellar continues to grow in tokenized assets, a major highlight of strong growth in Q3, 2026.

Sources indicate that real-world assets tokenized on Stellar amounted to $4.1 billion at the end of Q3 2026, up 36% from Q2 and up 548% from Q3 2025. Two assets drove the bulk of the quarter’s growth: Tradable’s upcoming tokenized private credit and continued inflows into the Spiko Amundi overnight swap fund.

In a recent development, in late August 2026, Stellar held more tokenized non-US government debt than any other blockchain, with about $490 million in sovereign instruments. These included Spiko’s euro Treasury bill fund, Mexican CETES and Brazilian Tesouro bonds through Etherfuse, South Korean Treasury bonds, and a Marshall Islands digital sovereign bond.

Stellar has widened access to tokenized funds in the United States, Europe and Asia. Franklin Templeton’s BENJI has been on Stellar since 2021. In August 2026, the SEC's Division of Investment Management issued a no-action letter confirming that the Franklin Templeton's registered mutual funds and ETFs may use BENJI for cash management. This expands the set of institutions permitted to hold it. Franklin Templeton made a similar move in Europe, registering 'grBenji' as a Luxembourg UCITS share class for third-party distribution, now live on 21X.

Sources indicate that in Asia, Marketnode announced in August that it will offer funds from BNY Investments on Stellar, with Marketnode acting as the tokenization and distribution platform. Together, these developments expand access to tokenized funds on Stellar for institutions in the United States, Europe and Asia.

State Street Investment Management and Galaxy brought their Onchain Liquidity Sweep Fund to Stellar in September 2026.

Bitcoin drops to $55K after $670M liquidations – What changes now?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, last week, Bitcoin [BTC] fell to a low of $55,130 on Saturday, the 20th of November.
  • It led to debate around whether the bear market was truly over, or whether what we saw in August-September was only a pause within the longer-term bearish trend.
  • Over the past two weeks, Bitcoin liquidations exceeded $600 million on four separate days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, last week, Bitcoin [BTC] fell to a low of $55,130 on Saturday, the 20th of November. This was lower than $57,800, which the leading crypto registered on the 1st of July.

It led to debate around whether the bear market was truly over, or whether what we saw in August-September was only a pause within the longer-term bearish trend.

Over the past two weeks, Bitcoin liquidations exceeded $600 million on four separate days.

The 11th and the 20th of November, when BTC breached key support levels at $73k and $61.4k, saw the heaviest long liquidations. Also, contextually speaking, these two days witnessed $690 million and $670 million in long liquidations, respectively.

The persistent downward price action was accompanied by relentless selling. Since the 5th of November, every trading day bar one has seen negative spot ETF flows.

Recent findings suggest that last week’s net outflows alone reached $1.245 billion. This incessant selling would need to ease before Bitcoin could find room to recover.

Recent findings suggest that as things stand, a weekly trading session close below $57,800 is needed to flip the structure bearishly. The previous week’s correction, though deep, might be just a liquidity sweep before a recovery.

Bitcoin holders are under severe strain as prices approach or drop below their cost basis, and Open Interest has plunged dramatically. It was a result of tightening monetary policy and the global equity market downturn.

Over the past year, the BTC Open Interest was down by $4.5 billion.

In July, this figure fell as low as $6.5 billion. It was the largest OI downturn in Bitcoin’s history in dollar terms, observed crypto analyst Darkfost.

There have been eight trading days in 2026 with over $1.5 billion in liquidations across the crypto market. A decline in risk appetite among investors, several liquidation cascades, and the overarching bearish price action for most of the year helped explain the OI drop.

A leverage reset can be healthy for the market.

Alongside the weekly BTC chart, there was hope for a bear market bottom. Even so, it remains risky to buy, as a bear market continuation cannot yet be fully ruled out.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that tesla’s “flying” Roadster just took a hit from Porsche.
  • Both automakers revealed their next halo cars on the same day, October 15.
  • In a recent development, tesla finally unveiled the next-gen Roadster last month, almost nine years after the 2017 prototype.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that tesla’s “flying” Roadster just took a hit from Porsche. Speaking at a conference in Berlin today, CEO Michael Leiters said Porsche wants “to completely steer clear from any kind of effects and shows,” according to Bloomberg.

Both automakers revealed their next halo cars on the same day, October 15. Tesla made a Roadster flip in mid-air. Porsche indicated the Mission S, and Leiters notes the two cars aren’t even chasing the same customers.

In a recent development, tesla finally unveiled the next-gen Roadster last month, almost nine years after the 2017 prototype. The main event was a car using compressed-air thrusters to launch off a ramp, rotate in the air, and come back down on its wheels.

It was the payoff for months of hype. Musk spent most of the year promising a “flying” Roadster demo, and it slipped more than once. We reported in June that it had been pushed to August to make room for SpaceX thruster work.

There are three versions. The Performance trim uses suction fans and claims 0-60 mph in under 1.6 seconds, the Thrust trim adds rear cold-gas thrusters for a claimed sub-0.9-second run, and the single-seat Rocket trim gets thrusters all around the car and isn’t approved for public roads. Tesla gave no price and no production date, just Musk’s “2028, actually.”.

Porsche went the other way. Under the skin, the Mission S can take either a hybrid or a straight combustion powertrain. It’s a mid-engine car that sits above the 911 in the lineup, and well above it in price.

Recent findings suggest that leiters noted customer response has been “overwhelming” and that Porsche would rather show off real technical innovation than put on a show. If it reaches production, Ferrari is the obvious target, and Porsche hasn’t played in that segment since the 918 Spyder. Porsche is counting on a pricier, more exclusive lineup to rebuild its profits.

Not everyone in the supercar world agrees with Leiters. Ferrari CEO Benedetto Vigna rated Tesla’s Roadster launch “10 out of 10” last month.

Leiters has a point, even if Porsche pitching a gas and hybrid supercar as “technical innovation” in 2026 is a bit rich. But what bothers me more is who Tesla is aiming at.

I’m concerned Tesla is starting to appeal to the lowest common denominator: people who watch a Roadster hop off a ramp and believe an actual flying car is coming. Musk pushed that idea himself. On Joe Rogan’s show, he called the upcoming demo “unforgettable” and said that if Peter Thiel wants a flying car, “we should be able to buy one.”.

Industry observers note that that’s not real. Cold-gas thrusters work like a giant can of compressed air, and the math is brutal. The Rocket trim carries 400 liters of air at 10,000 psi, roughly 200 kg of gas. At the roughly 80 kN its rear thrusters produce, even a very efficient nozzle empties that tank in a few seconds. Then refilling it takes six to seven hours.

Also someone on Bluesky pointed out that the video indicates Mach diamonds in the exhaust stream of the thrusters. Which means it's so loud that anyone within 100 feet would suffer immediate and permanent hearing loss. This Roadster isn't useful for anything other than temporarily pumping stock prices.

Recent findings suggest that so the Roadster’s “flying” will always be limited to stunts like this one. No hopping over traffic. No hovering. A couple of seconds of air, then a long wait at a compressor.

Sources indicate that that’s great for a viral clip. But this is a car that dropped from a promised 620 miles of range in 2017 to “over 300” today, and Tesla would rather sell people on a flight the physics can’t deliver.

It has been revealed that it’s hard for me to get excited for that. As a BEV enthusiast, I’m not more excited about Porsche’s ICE Mission S, but at least I trust Porsche to actually deliver that to customers.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota and Subaru’s newly introduced electric SUVs are catching on with buyers, offering various options and prices ranging from about $35,000 to $45,000, or the “sweet spot” of the US market.
  • The US electric vehicle market rebounded in the third quarter with 262,649 EVs sold, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates, up 6.1% from Q2 and the strongest performance of the year.
  • Although nearly every automaker has sold fewer EVs so far this year than in the same period in 2025, as buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, a handful of brands are seeing considerably higher demand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota and Subaru’s newly introduced electric SUVs are catching on with buyers, offering various options and prices ranging from about $35,000 to $45,000, or the “sweet spot” of the US market.

The US electric vehicle market rebounded in the third quarter with 262,649 EVs sold, according to Kelley Blue Book estimates, up 6.1% from Q2 and the strongest performance of the year.

Although nearly every automaker has sold fewer EVs so far this year than in the same period in 2025, as buyers rushed to claim the $7,500 tax credit before it expired, a handful of brands are seeing considerably higher demand.

Outside of Rivian, Toyota and Subaru are the only brands that have higher year-over-year EV sales in the US through the third quarter.

Combined, Toyota and Subaru have sold nearly 50,000 EVs through the first nine months of 2026, more than double compared to the same period last year.

In a recent development, toyota alone has sold nearly 35,000 electric vehicles, up 183.4% YOY, while Subaru sold 14,630, up 46.7%. And that’s not even including the additional 12,676 sold under the Lexus brand, up 137.4% YOY.

While the two Japanese automakers were infamously slow to transition to battery electric vehicles, the timing worked in their favor.

Recent findings suggest that after launching the heavily updated bZ in late 2025, previously called the bZ4X, Toyota’s electric SUV suddenly became one of America’s most popular EVs. Through Q3, it was the fourth best-selling EV in the US, trailing only the Hyundai IONIQ 5, Tesla Model 3, and Tesla Model Y.

Starting at $35,000, the Toyota bZ is one of the most affordable EVs in the US. It also offers up to 314 miles of range in the FWD Plus trim, which starts at $37,980.

Toyota and Subaru now each sell three electric SUVs, which share the same platform and technology.

With prices ranging from roughly $35,000 to about $45,000, Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, said (via Bloomberg) Toyota and Subaru’s fresh EVs are affordable and hit the “sweet spot” of the US car market.

Toyota also sells the smaller, sporty C-HR, starting at $37,080, and the larger, more rugged bZ Woodland, which starts at $45,380.

Subaru, on the other hand, sells the updated Solterra ($38,495, plus the smaller Uncharted ($34,995) and midsize Trailseeker ($39,995).

Karla Fisher, a Marine and retired engineer, told Bloomberg that the Subaru Trailseeker was her “most favorite car of all time.”.

Industry observers note that while she considered buying an EV before the $7,500 federal credit expired last September, none met her requirements at the time. Fisher wanted at least 7″ of ground clearance, 250 miles or more range, and a price that was similar, or even less than a comparible gas-powered vehicle.

The Subaru Trailseeker offers all of that and starts at under $40,000. Toyota and Subaru’s electric SUVs all start at about $45,000 or less, which is even less than the average latest vehicle.

According to the latest Kelley Blue Book figures, the average price for a fresh vehicle in the US reached a record $51,109 in October, up 2.1% YOY.

Great as these may be, there is little inventory to be found.

There are less than 500 Uncharted available Nationwide.

You can't sell what you don't have. Yes, they can be ordered for sure, but how many missed sales does that model create?

Subaru spokesperson Dominick Infante said the affordable EV prices are mainly thanks to its partnership with Toyota. “We do believe there’s an EV future,” Infante added.

Next year, both brands will add a three-row electric SUV with the Toyota Highlander EV and Subaru Getaway.

Sources indicate that thinking about making the switch to an EV? With the 2027 models at dealerships, now could be a good time to find a deal on current 2026 models. You can use the links below to see what’s available at Toyota and Subaru dealerships near you.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt has softened the tone of his recent Bitcoin warnings and remarked on X that the cryptocurrency held at the level it needed to hold after its drop to $55,150 over the weekend.

"Bitcoin held exactly where it had to hold -- for now anyway, but perhaps for more than now," Brandt wrote on Monday.

According to recent reports, brandt also shared a monthly chart of Bitcoin together with the post. The chart goes back to 2018, and Brandt marked on it the same patterns that he had already pointed to in previous years. According to the chart, the price of Bitcoin was back above $63,000 at the time of the post and stood at $63,338.

Recent findings suggest that on Saturday, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150. It was the lowest price of the cryptocurrency since September 2024, and before that, the lowest price of Bitcoin in 2026 was $57,718 on July 1, according to Coinbase.

In a recent development, on Nov. 15, Brandt posted a weekly chart with a possible head-and-shoulders top and mentioned that, if the pattern proves valid, Bitcoin's October 2025 record of about $126,000 may not be surpassed in his lifetime. Two days before that, on Nov. 13, Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time since August.

Industry observers note that brandt has also pointed to the history of Bitcoin's bull market cycles more than once. Late last year, he posted a chart showing that each of Bitcoin's five major bull runs began after drawdowns of 75% or more, and he wrote that if the decline carried to $50,000, "the next bull market cycle should carry to $200k to $250K.".

In a recent development, in April, Brandt noted that Bitcoin could form an "investable low" in September or October 2026. According to Brandt, this low may or may not go below the February low near $60,000, and the next cycle peak could land between $300,000 and $500,000 in September or October 2029 if the four-year cycle continues to hold.

"Real bottom will not occur until October 2026," Brandt remarked in an interview in February.

Industry observers note that the latest Brandt post comes amid a rally in U.S. tech stocks on Monday. Earlier that day, Nvidia announced that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately.

According to the Nvidia announcement, the board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government before the decision, and it is confident that Huang's return "poses no national security risk." Shares of Nvidia surged 33% after the news, according to CNBC.

Bitcoin went up together with tech stocks and briefly climbed above $64,000 on Monday. Before the Nvidia news, Bitcoin had already recovered from the Saturday low to around $61,500.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12. On Nov. 17, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones stated on the company's earnings call that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Hyundai announced its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the latest IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.
  • While Hyundai discontinued the standard IONIQ 6, it added the high-performance IONIQ 6 N for the 2027 lineup.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai’s US electric vehicle lineup will look a bit different in 2027, including the newly introduced IONIQ 6 N, a new range-topping IONIQ 9 trim, and a handful of minor updates to the IONIQ 5.

Hyundai announced its 2027 model-year changes on Wednesday, including the latest IONIQ 6 N and a few slight changes to the IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9.

While Hyundai discontinued the standard IONIQ 6, it added the high-performance IONIQ 6 N for the 2027 lineup.

According to recent reports, the IONIQ 6 N is Hyundai’s second performance EV, following the IONIQ 5 N. Powered by a dual-motor all-wheel-drive powertrain, the electric sports car delivers a combined 641 hp and 568 lb-ft of torque.

Hyundai said the IONIQ 6 N can sprint from 0 to 60 mph in 3.2 seconds, beating the IONIQ 5 N at 3.25 seconds.

Like the IONIQ 5 N, it also includes fun added features, like N e-Shift and an N Active Sound+ system that simulates the sounds and sensations of a traditional gas-powered sports car with an 8-speed dual-clutch transmission.

It uses an 84 kWh battery that provides up to 245 miles of pure electric driving range. Thanks to its 800V ultra-fast charging architecture, the IONIQ 6 N can charge from 10% to 80% in about 18 minutes using a 350 kW DC fast charger.

Like Hyundai’s other electric vehicles, it comes standard with a native NACS charging port and a CCS adapter.

The 2027 IONIQ 5 and IONIQ 9 are mostly carryover models with a few minor changes, while the IONIQ 5 N remains the same as the 2026 model year.

Changes to the IONIQ 5 for the 2027 model year include roof rails, which are now available on the SEL trim and above; previously, they were only available on the XRT and Limited trims.

Hyundai HomeLink will be available exclusively on the Limited trim, rather than SEL and above, in the current 2026 model year, while the Cargo Cover will be offered as an Accessory only.

Regarding color options, the Gravity Gold Matte and Sage Silver Matte will no longer be available for the 2027 IONIQ 5.

The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 starts at $35,250, making it one of the most affordable EVs in the US.

It has been revealed that that’s for the standard-range IONIQ 5 SE with an EPA-estimated range of up to 245 miles. The extended-range SE RWD model is $2,500 more, starting at $37,750, and offers up to 318 miles of range.

Hyundai’s three-row SUV also received a handful of updates. The 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 9 will be available with a newly introduced Calligraphy Black Ink trim, while the Calligraphy Design will no longer be offered.

The 2027 IONIQ 9 Calligraphy and Calligraphy Black Ink trims gain a Virtual Gear Shift and heated third-row seats. All variants also gain a Tailgate Emergency Lamp.

On the one hand... the Ioniq5 is due for an revision. On the other... I still absolutely love the way it looks, and notice just about every one I pass on the road.

Hyundai has yet to announce prices for the 2027 model. The base 2026 IONIQ 9 S starts at $58,995 and offers an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 335 miles.

The previous top-spec Performance Calligraphy Design AWD started at $76,490, so you can expect the upcoming Calligraphy Black Ink to be around the same, if not even more.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the foundation said its Peg Stability Module kept exchanging USDS for USDC at one-for-one throughout the day.
  • The reserve fell from 2.56 billion USDC earlier on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holders swapped more than $2 billion of Sky’s USDS for USDC on Nov. 19, according to Sky Frontier Foundation. Sky’s Ethereum reserve for one-for-one swaps fell by about two-thirds in hours. At 17:55 UTC it held 867 million USDC, the amount immediately available to USDS and DAI holders using the shared pool. Seconds later, a debt repayment in Sky’s Obex allocation vault put about 100 million USDC back into the pool.

In a recent development, the foundation said its Peg Stability Module kept exchanging USDS for USDC at one-for-one throughout the day. The reported $2 billion-plus was gross volume in that direction.

The reserve fell from 2.56 billion USDC earlier on Nov. 19 to 867 million USDC before the Obex repayment, a net decline of 1.69 billion USDC. The foundation’s gross figure counts trades in one direction. The balance change reflects USDC moving both ways.

Industry observers note that the foundation remarked the reserve stayed at or above 800 million USDC and later crossed 1.1 billion on Nov. 20. The 867 million reading comes from Ethereum block 26450759, 24 seconds before the Obex repayment. At 12:38 UTC on Nov. 23, Sky’s PSM dashboard showed 1.76 billion USDC, just over twice the pre-repayment balance.

Recent findings suggest that the reserve fell to 867 million USDC shortly before 17:56 UTC on Nov. 19. Four on-chain balances show the drawdown and partial recovery.

Source: Early Nov. 19 · 17:41 balance · Pre-refill balance · 17:41 block · Transfer records · 19:10 balance · Nov. 20 balance.

Sky’s LitePSM guide explains how the Ethereum module serves both tokens. A DAI holder can trade directly. For a USDS holder, a separate contract converts USDS to DAI inside the same transaction and pays out USDC from the same reserve. The module keeps those USDC tokens at a separate address called the pocket.

At 15:48 UTC on Nov. 19, a holder exchanged 400 million USDS for 400 million USDC. The USDS was burned, the equivalent amount of DAI went into the module, and the pocket sent the holder USDC.

That shared inventory sets a ceiling for both tokens. A holder can take out only as much USDC as is available when the trade executes. Other swaps can change that amount within the same block. Governance can set fees or pause either direction. The one-for-one rate describes trades through the module itself. Sky has also integrated USDS and USDC routing with Uniswap, where Uniswap swap fees can depend on the route. Holders who want bank dollars after the exchange still need a separate USDC redemption route.

It has been revealed that at 17:55:47 UTC, an Obex repayment sent about 100 million USDC into the pocket. In the same transaction, the module released an equal amount of DAI, which was converted to USDS and used to repay debt in the Obex vault.

At 19:00 UTC, another holder swapped 12 million USDC for 12 million USDS, sending USDC into the reserve.

Two November 19 transactions added USDC to the same pool. Each sent the USDS proceeds to a different destination.

The Obex trade paid down an allocation loan. The ordinary swap issued USDS to its sender.

In a recent development, these two inflows are examples from the recovery window. The earlier source of Obex’s USDC and the full breakdown of the rebound remain unresolved.

Follow USDC and USDS transfers and the Obex vault repayment event in the November 19 Ethereum transaction records. The graphic rounds the larger amount to the nearest thousand USDC.

These two inflows are examples from the recovery window. The earlier source of Obex’s USDC and the full breakdown of the rebound remain unresolved.

Recent findings suggest that it held 1.13 billion USDC around 17:20 UTC on Nov. 20, about 260 million USDC above the pre-repayment balance.

It has been revealed that at 17:41 UTC on Nov. 19, about 14 minutes before the Obex repayment, the pocket held 872 million USDC. At that same block, Ethereum had 6.92 billion issued USDS and DAI after subtracting the DAI already held in the module’s own buffer. The USDC available could cover 12.6% of that adjusted Ethereum supply at one-for-one.

Sources indicate that sky Frontier Foundation put protocol-wide collateral at about $9.3 billion on Nov. 20. That figure describes backing across Sky. For a holder looking to convert through LitePSM, the relevant balance is the USDC in the pocket.

In the Nov. 23 dashboard reading, the reserve stood at 28.3% of circulating USDS and DAI, below Sky’s 30% target. That ratio uses the dashboard’s definition of circulating supply. Sky’s stUSDS vault withdrawals depend on available USDS. Vault holders must redeem for USDS before using the swap module.

#156019. Tech Report: Tesla confirms rare new delivery of 50 Semi electric trucks in Chicago

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1053 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Tesla confirms rare new delivery of 50 Semi electric trucks in Chicago

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1053 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has confirmed a latest batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.
  • Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its new Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.
  • The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, indicates four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has confirmed a latest batch of Tesla Semi deliveries, with its official Semi account saying today that “Chicago’s first 50 Semis” are on their way to the city.

It’s a rare data point. Tesla doesn’t disclose Semi deliveries, and it claims its new Nevada factory can build 50,000 of them a year.

The post, published on the @tesla_semi account on X at noon ET today, indicates four Semis lined up at sunset under the caption “Hello Windy City.” Tesla didn’t name the customer.

Hello Windy CityChicago’s first 50 Semis en route for delivery pic.twitter.com/75kig8yWsb.

According to recent reports, but the only 50-truck Semi order tied to Chicago belongs to HMD Trucking. The family-owned carrier was founded in Chicago in 1998, runs more than 650 trucks (almost all diesel), and ordered 50 Semis right after Tesla’s production event in September.

Sources indicate that HMD took its first truck on November 2 and says it’s the first Tesla Semi registered in Illinois. COO Michael Mahler said Tesla “has been transparent with us regarding the capabilities of Semi every step of the way.”.

The company ran a Semi for more than 4,000 miles over the summer and averaged 1.74 kWh per mile, right in line with Tesla’s 1.7 kWh/mile claim. The first trucks will mostly handle local runs around Chicago, and HMD is installing its own chargers there since Tesla’s Megacharger network is still concentrated along the I-5 and I-10 corridors in the West.

Owner Henry Malukas told MotorTrend the deal is worth about $15 million. That’s roughly $300,000 per truck, in line with the ~$290,000 Long Range pricing we reported when the first truck came off the high-volume line and a long way from the $180,000 Tesla advertised in 2017.

Here’s the problem: it’s nearly impossible to tell how many Semis Tesla is actually building.

According to recent reports, tesla launched volume production at its Sparks, Nevada factory on September 24, after pushing the ramp out of 2025. It states the 1.8 million sq ft plant is built for 50,000 trucks a year. But it never gave a ramp schedule, and its quarterly production and delivery reports only count “passenger vehicles sold to customers.” The Semi isn’t in there.

So we’re left with proxies. Tesla notes its Semi fleet has over 98% uptime, without saying how big that fleet is. Before this year, the largest Semi fleet was PepsiCo’s, at 86 trucks in 2024. California’s truck voucher program received 965 Semi applications between January 2025 and February 2026, which points to real demand but says nothing about output.

It has been revealed that the order book is the other clue. Einride ordered 500 Semis in August, WattEV has 370 on order, IMC Logistics wants 50 for California, and the ZET SCALE alliance picked Tesla as main supplier for 2,500 trucks. And now HMD’s 50 are rolling into Chicago, one of the first Semi fleets that will have to deal with a Midwest winter. Wisconsin’s Paper Transport has also been piloting a Semi in the Chicago market since the summer.

None of that adds up to a production rate, but it does look like Tesla is slowly ramping up deliveries.

Tesla keeps the Semi numbers vague on purpose. It’s happy to talk about a 50,000-truck-a-year factory, and it posts hero shots when a batch ships, but it won’t give the one number that shows whether the factory is anywhere close to that.

In a recent development, I think the semi is going to be a big seller but its going to take some time to produce enough of them and for companies to gather enough data. Once the investment is justified, there will be customers and repeat customers. After that, it will only be a matter of time before other electric semi truck manufacturers start popping up with offerings and thats a good thing for everyone.

The 50,000 figure is what makes the Semi look like a real business to investors instead of a niche program that took nine years to get going. Tesla has a long history of quoting capacity long before it reaches it, so we shouldn’t treat “built for 50,000” as anything more than a ceiling.

According to recent reports, our read: Tesla is still far from that 50,000 rate. Fifty trucks for one customer is 0.1% of a year at full capacity, and if Tesla were shipping in large volumes, a single 50-unit batch wouldn’t get its own post. But the ramp has clearly started, the order book is real, and it’s plausible Tesla gets into the thousands by the end of the year.

It has been revealed that good for HMD, too. A 650-truck diesel fleet in a cold market is exactly the kind of customer the Semi has to win. Malukas admitted “we don’t have real numbers yet” on savings, and HMD’s own blog is fairly sober about cost and winter range. Local routes, depot charging and a Chicago winter is the right way to find out. It all sounds plausible for the Tesla Semi.

Despite the sharp fall in the cryptocurrency market, Michael Saylor-led Strategy has not stopped its Bitcoin (BTC) buying spree, as it picked up 457 BTC worth around $29.6 million.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

The latest data from Strategy's SEC filing reveals that the firm has bought 457 Bitcoin at an average price of $64,898 per coin.

The fresh purchase brings Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings to around 851,305 BTC, which accounts for over 4% of the cryptocurrency's maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The firm has now spent around $64.23 billion to build its Bitcoin holdings at an average price of $75,446 per Bitcoin.

It is worth noting that Strategy has been buying BTC at gradually decreasing prices as the cryptocurrency market continues to bleed heavily.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 2, the firm declared that it had bought 811 BTC, worth around $65.5 million, at an average price of $80,846 per Bitcoin.

A week later, on Nov. 9, Strategy confirmed the purchase of 1,036 BTC worth $81.9 million at an average price of $79,012.

The firm’s Bitcoin purchase a week later, on Nov. 16, was relatively smaller at 485 BTC, worth $33.4 million, with an average price of $68,887.

Industry observers note that the new 457 BTC purchase continues this pattern. The latest Strategy purchase was made at an almost 20% lower price than the firm’s Nov. 2 acquisition.

Overall, the firm has made four weekly purchases, scooping up around 2,789 BTC worth $210.4 million.

According to recent reports, however, these purchases have been much smaller than before. The latest $29.6 million purchase is almost 64% lower than the $81.9 million purchase announced just two weeks ago.

Although Saylor is doubling down on Bitcoin, Strategy’s massive holdings in the cryptocurrency are underwater as the market has been struggling to regain its footing.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 21, Bitcoin hit a low of around $55,130, its lowest level since September 2024, before rebounding above $61,000.

The firm’s recent purchases have helped reduce its overall average Bitcoin acquisition cost, but the drop has not been that significant.

For example, with the latest purchase, the average cost of the firm’s Bitcoin holdings dropped from $75,452 to around $75,446, a decline of just $6 per Bitcoin.

At the same time, the firm has also been putting a lot of resources into supporting its preferred securities.

In the latest reporting period, Strategy sold around 1.93 million common shares, raising net proceeds of $176.7 million.

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP ETF Shares Surface in Schwab’s Repo Collateral.

XRP ETF shares just appeared in collateral baskets pledged by JPMorgan & Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund.

XRP exchange-traded fund shares appeared in collateral baskets posted by JPMorgan and Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund, according to wealth coach Kamilah Stevenson.

In her latest YouTube episode, she argues that the reported holdings point to a less visible source of institutional demand: securities pledged against loans rather than bought for price exposure.

According to recent reports, the distinction matters. Stevenson says Schwab did not buy XRP or the ETFs outright; its fund lent cash and received baskets of securities backing the transactions.

Citing monthly SEC disclosures, Stevenson identifies XRP ETF shares from Grayscale, Canary, Franklin and Bitwise among collateral supplied by the banks’ trading arms.

She puts their combined value at roughly $36,000 in April, $2 million in June and more than $8 million by August, an increase exceeding 200-fold.

Those figures remain claims presented in the video. The transcript does not specify the reporting year or filing identifiers, limiting verification of the sequence.

Stevenson acknowledges that the positions were small relative to the underlying loans. Their inclusion would demonstrate acceptance of particular ETF securities within collateral baskets, not necessarily an institutional commitment to holding XRP directly.

The YouTube video episode connects those reported positions to BlackRock’s effort to expand acceptance of tokenized fund shares as collateral. Dr. Stevenson says the appeal is straightforward: investors could pledge income-producing fund shares instead of redeeming them to provide cash.

Recent findings suggest that she also points to Binance’s acceptance of BlackRock’s BUIDL fund as collateral and describes a wider shift toward blockchain-based collateral transfers. Her thesis is that assets used to secure financing can generate more persistent demand than assets held solely for trading.

“Trading creates excitement; collateral creates demand that stays,” Dr. Stevenson states.

Sources indicate that that argument needs a boundary. Acceptance of XRP ETF shares does not establish that lenders accept XRP itself, and tokenized collateral does not automatically require XRP to move between markets. Stevenson presents direct XRP-backed lending and cross-currency settlement as potential next steps, not completed developments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him crack the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old puzzle with a $1 million prize attached.

His claim surfaced Friday, one day after the AI company’s stock-market debut, and has not yet been independently verified.

According to recent reports, “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpöge wrote in a four-page note. He notes the method also resolves the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, which extends the question to other mathematical functions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

In a recent development, alpöge says he and Claude encoded their argument in Lean, software used to check mathematical proofs step by step. His note links to 14 downloadable parts of the proof archive, but its availability does not amount to acceptance by the mathematical community.

Alpöge says he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about a possible announcement “late Sunday night,” November 15. He then consulted company leadership and stated there was a constraint to respect, without explaining precisely what it was.

Recent findings suggest that “The precise timing is horrible,” he acknowledged. Alpöge rejected a cynical interpretation of the timing, but did not explicitly say the company’s IPO caused the delay.

Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq Thursday, November 19, after raising $81.34 billion in its offering.

Alpöge figured in September’s AI math wars. OpenAI claimed it had solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem as he and NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster pursued related fluid-equation work, sparking a credit dispute over research priority.

Industry observers note that openAI followed in October with 722 manuscripts generated by an unreleased model, grouped into 372 families of results. Only 162 included Lean-checked main results, and mathematicians demanded stronger evidence rather than accepting the organization’s flood of claims at face value.

Some mathematicians fear a “mathocalypse,” with AI solving coveted problems before researchers can learn from pursuing them. Toronto mathematician Daniel Litt warned that, without adaptation, “there’s just no more math in 50 years.” At an MIT panel this week, Buckmaster argued mathematics still requires human understanding.

Industry observers note that first posed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis predicts where certain zeros of the Riemann zeta function fall. The question matters because those zeros are linked to the distribution of prime numbers, whose patterns underlie extensive mathematical research.

A proof would be a historic mathematical result, since experts have been trying to solve that for over a century.

Recent findings suggest that lean can verify that formal deductions obey its rules. Mathematicians still need to reproduce the archive, check the formalized theorem matches the original conjecture, and examine the claimed result before considering it settled.

Anthropic previously reported progress on the zeta function without claiming to solve the full hypothesis. Alpöge’s new assertion goes far beyond that earlier work.

In a recent development, the Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Riemann hypothesis among its Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million award. Under the institute’s prize rules, a proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, survive at least two years of scrutiny, and earn general acceptance before the prize can be considered.

That mentioned, the combined holdings of participants reportedly fell from $148 million in May 2025 to just $8.6 million for the latest gala.

Remarking on the same, Donald Sherman, president of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington ( CREW), remarked,.

Donald Trump’s memecoin dinner is the clearest evidence that he cares more about lining his pockets and giving access to his personal investors than addressing the problems facing the American public.

That mentioned, the controversy goes beyond the declining price of a cryptocurrency. This is because the Democrats argue that Trump is using his position as president to financially benefit from businesses connected to his personal brand.

The concern is that investors may have purchased $TRUMP tokens not simply because of the memecoin itself, but because holding them could give them insider access.

Recent findings suggest that needless to say, eight Democratic senators, led by Adam Schiff, have already questioned Trump and his crypto ventures thanks to the insider activity and profit-making. As expected, they have also called for investigations into his crypto-related businesses.

On Monday, XRP briefly rose above $1 after the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia sparked a rally on Wall Street and a wave of short liquidations in the crypto market. At the peak of the move, short liquidations on XRP exceeded long liquidations by 578%, according to CoinGlass data.

On the XRPUSDT perpetual contract on Binance, the price of XRP went from $0.94 to as high as $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, and later it pulled back and stood at $0.984, according to TradingView.

Earlier on Monday, before the opening bell, Nvidia revealed that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. The tech giant said that the board was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings with him, and that its independent investigation would continue. According to the company, the board received input from senior U.S. government officials and concluded that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones remarked in a statement.

Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and on Nov. 17, during the company's earnings call, Jones said that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

Industry observers note that in premarket trading, Nvidia stock jumped 27% to $159.48 as of 9 a.m. ET, and at the start of U.S. trading on Monday, Nvidia shares were up more than 30%. The rally spread across Wall Street, and the S&P 500 rose as much as 5.6% and the Nasdaq 100 as much as 7.9%, according to NBC News.

CoinGlass data demonstrates that $9.45 million worth of XRP positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and $7.18 million of that amount came from short positions. Long positions accounted for $2.27 million.

The same happened across the rest of the crypto market. In total, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGlass, and shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

Bitcoin led the list with $273.26 million in liquidations, and 82.8% of that amount came from short positions. Ethereum followed with $139.07 million, and Solana was third with $24.93 million.

Besides, perpetual contracts on Nvidia stock and on SOXL, a triple-leveraged exchange-traded fund on semiconductor stocks, were next on the list with $16.34 million and $15.01 million in liquidations, respectively, according to CoinGlass.

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1108 w)

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla extends Cybertruck production to late summer 2027 amid fan backlash

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk now indicates Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first confirmed it was killing it.
  • The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it states about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.
  • Sources indicate that on November 6, Musk mentioned Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk now indicates Tesla will keep building the Cybertruck “through the end of summer 2027” to “work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog.” That buys the electric pickup roughly two to three more months, five days after Tesla first confirmed it was killing it.

The reprieve lands as a growing number of Tesla’s own fans push back on the decision, and on what it states about Tesla’s future as a company that sells cars to people.

Sources indicate that on November 6, Musk mentioned Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas “around the middle of next year” to make room for Cybercab. On November 9, he wrote the line would shut “in about 8 months” and that Tesla would “have to return deposits for a lot of people.” Now it’s the end of summer.

In order to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog, production will be extended through the end of summer 2027.

The reasons have moved around just as much. First it was factory space, then “a very limited number of smart, dedicated people,” then the “opportunity cost” of the truck’s complexity. We went through each of them: Tesla is ending the Cybertruck as sales stall at about 10% of plan, Musk’s demand claim doesn’t survive the numbers, and Musk admitted Tesla doesn’t have the talent to run more than one vehicle program.

Sources indicate that and the “backlog” is one Tesla built itself. Before the announcement, the truck was selling at a pace of roughly 30,000 units a year, about 10% of the 250,000 Tesla planned for, on a line with over 125,000 units of installed capacity. Telling people the truck is going away creates a last-call rush. That’s not demand Tesla was missing before.

Sources indicate that tesla also raised Cybertruck prices by up to 10% the same day and paused orders for the base Dual Motor. The cheapest Cybertruck you can order is now $92,490, up from $69,990 in early August.

According to recent reports, some of the people in that backlog have been waiting a while. Several cheering in Musk’s replies say they’re still waiting on the $59,990 Cybertruck Tesla sold for “10 days only” in February. One asked whether Tesla will prioritize Premium and Cyberbeast orders over theirs. Musk didn’t answer.

Industry observers note that the most telling replies weren’t about the truck. Chuck Cook, one of the best-known FSD testers in the Tesla community, quote-tweeted Musk asking him to “change your mind,” adding: “Cybercab won’t haul my bees.”.

Another longtime Tesla supporter, Phil Trubey, asked for “a vehicle roadmap post end of summer 2027,” followed by: “Will Tesla make any other vehicle?”.

Recent findings suggest that that’s the right question, and Tesla hasn’t revealed a single new consumer vehicle to answer it. Tesla started 2026 with five consumer vehicle programs: Model S, Model X, Model 3, Model Y, and Cybertruck. It ended Model S and Model X production in the spring, citing “autonomy.” The Cybertruck goes next. By fall 2027, Tesla’s consumer lineup will be the Model 3 and Model Y, two vehicles that rolled out in 2017 and 2020.

In a recent development, tesla’s answer to the affordable car it promised for years was stripped-down “Standard” versions of those same two vehicles. In China, its second-biggest market, Tesla turned Giga Shanghai into an export hub, and domestic retail sales crashed 66% in October to the lowest level in over four years.

Even Unplugged Performance, the biggest Tesla tuner around, offered to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands and pay a license fee. People want this truck built. Tesla doesn’t.

We’ve been warning about this for years, and for years we got called haters for it.

According to recent reports, the pattern has been clear since Tesla swapped its affordable car prepares for Robotaxi in 2024. No upcoming consumer platform. Model S and X killed “for autonomy.” Cybertruck killed “for Cybercab.” A Roadster pitched as a thruster stunt nine years after its unveiling. Every product decision points away from selling cars to people and toward robotaxis and Optimus, two businesses that don’t generate meaningful revenue today.

I am beginning to suspect that Elon does not always tell the truth.

As long as we have an economic climate that allows massive amounts of money to be made off of speculation as opposed to actual product, future bots and robotaxis have a great deal of value whether they actually become viable or not.

In a recent development, A two-to-three-month extension doesn’t change any of that. It’s a gesture to the loudest part of the fan base, and it happens to let Tesla sell a few thousand more trucks at prices up to 10% higher than last week. Fine. But the people who bought into Tesla’s mission to accelerate the world’s transition to sustainable energy are now realizing that mission was quietly rewritten, and the word “sustainable” didn’t make the cut.

Tesla is becoming a organization that sells two aging EVs to fund a bet on autonomy. That might work out for shareholders. We have our doubts, given Tesla is still behind Waymo by every public metric. But it’s a lot less exciting for the people who wanted the next great Tesla car.

The question for fans now: when the Model 3 and Model Y get their own “opportunity cost” post on X, will anyone actually be surprised?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The rally put the chipmaker on course for the largest single-day market capitalization gain in stock market history, reversing part of the selloff triggered by Huang's resignation less than two weeks earlier.
  • The Kobeissi Letter noted that NVIDIA's shares initially climbed more than 28%, adding approximately $820 billion to its market capitalization, before extending gains above 35% and pushing the increase past $1 trillion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that NVIDIA added about $1 trillion in market value on Nov. 23 as its shares surged more than 35% after the unexpected reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

The rally put the chipmaker on course for the largest single-day market capitalization gain in stock market history, reversing part of the selloff triggered by Huang's resignation less than two weeks earlier.

The Kobeissi Letter noted that NVIDIA's shares initially climbed more than 28%, adding approximately $820 billion to its market capitalization, before extending gains above 35% and pushing the increase past $1 trillion.

If sustained through the closing bell, the increase would establish a new record for the largest amount of market value added by a publicly traded organization in a single session.

The gains followed NVIDIA's announcement that its board had unanimously reinstated Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.

Directors said discussions with Huang had satisfied them about his ability to lead the manufacturer. The board also consulted senior US government officials before concluding that his reinstatement posed no national security risk.

According to recent reports, the decision reversed NVIDIA's Nov. 12 leadership shake-up, which had intensified selling across technology stocks and cryptocurrencies.

The rebound extended beyond NVIDIA, with the Nasdaq advancing more than 6% and the S&P 500 gaining approximately 5% in early trading.

Cryptocurrencies also rallied as traders rapidly increased their exposure to riskier assets. Bitcoin surged more than 4% within an hour of the announcement, reaching $64,427 after briefly falling below $60,000 during the previous week's selloff.

However, smaller cryptocurrencies recorded even stronger gains.

Glassnode reported that altcoins led the market's initial response to Huang's reinstatement. Within 20 minutes of the announcement, nearly every cryptocurrency among the 50 largest was outperforming Bitcoin.

The analytics firm observed the rally spread from altcoins to the Nasdaq and Bitcoin, while the S&P 500 posted a smaller advance.

The rapid rotation showed how swiftly appetite for speculative assets returned following the leadership reversal at the world's leading AI chipmaker.

The reinstatement also produced a dramatic reversal in prediction-market pricing.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 16, CryptoSlate previously reported that Polymarket traders assigned Huang only a 6% probability of returning to NVIDIA by Nov. 30, despite growing pressure from prominent technology executives and investors.

It has been revealed that at the time, the probability of a return by Dec. 31 stood at 14%, while the longer-dated contract covering December 2027 carried a 38% probability.

According to recent reports, however, those expectations changed significantly following NVIDIA's announcement. By Nov. 23, the November contract had climbed to 99.3%, before reaching 100% on Polymarket's market page.

Combined trading volume across the four contracts reached approximately $12.34 million, reflecting heightened interest in the leadership crisis.

Two quotes on the same Polymarket contract for a formal return to NVIDIA.

Huang’s executive roles and board seat qualify under the event rules.

The bars compare two dated observations.

Recent findings suggest that both bars use the same zero-based 0% to 100% scale. Length is proportional to the reported Yes quote. The dated points come from CryptoSlate’s Nov. 16 article and its Nov. 23 14:37 UTC market snapshot.

The bars compare two dated observations.

The November contract accounted for $5.75 million, while the December contract attracted another $5.62 million. The remaining volume came from contracts covering March and December 2027.

The sharp repricing illustrates how strongly traders had discounted Huang's prospects of returning before the end of November, only for NVIDIA's board to reverse its earlier decision.

Under Polymarket's resolution rules, Huang needed to return to NVIDIA in a formal executive, advisory, or governance capacity before the relevant deadline.

His reinstatement as both chief executive and director satisfies those conditions, turning what had been considered an unlikely outcome into a confirmed corporate development.

Tech Report: BYD’s full-size luxury SUV has a wheel problem, and it’s fixing it for free

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its new full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels.
  • The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.
  • According to recent reports, after opening preorders at the Beijing Auto Show in April, BYD said the high-end SUV secured over 30,000 preorders in 24 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is apologizing after a supplier error left some owners of its new full-size flagship SUV with the wrong wheels.

The Great Tang, or Da Tang as it’s called in China, is the first flagship D-segment SUV under its Dynasty series, the largest and most luxurious SUV from the lineup.

According to recent reports, after opening preorders at the Beijing Auto Show in April, BYD said the high-end SUV secured over 30,000 preorders in 24 hours. Two weeks later, preorders reached over 100,000.

By the time it went on sale in mid-June, over 150,000 buyers had preordered the Great Tang, marking a newly introduced record for a single BYD model.

While it has been the top-selling pure electric large SUV for two months, with more than 10,000 sold since it hit the market, BYD issued an apology on November 11 for fitting the wrong front and rear wheel rims on some Great Tang models.

The apology comes after several owners complained that the wheels were improperly installed on their vehicles.

BYD said the matter stemmed from a coding error by the wheel mesh assembly supplier, which led to incorrect assembly on some Great Tang vehicles.

It has been revealed that the tech giant said it “immediately” launched an investigation and corrected the problem so newly built vehicles will not be affected. In addition, the supplier introduced a new visual error-prevention mechanism to limit challenges like this going forward.

BYD said the problem does not affect the vehicle’s handling or pose a safety risk during driving.

The company mentioned owners can take affected vehicles to their local service center for a free inspection and professional wheel rim replacement. It’s also offering a replacement vehicle or compensation for transportation expenses.

Effective immediately, BYD said, the warranty on affected Great Tang vehicles will also be restarted.

Sources indicate that the Great Tang is on sale in China in pure electric (EV) and plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrains. The cheapest Premium EV variant starts at 239,900 yuan ($35,500).

Sources indicate that all versions use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries. While the base Premium model uses a 105.79 kWh battery, the Flagship EV trim uses a larger 130.15 kWh battery that delivers up to 590 miles (950 km) of CLTC range. It starts at 269,900 yuan ($40,000).

The Great Tang is huge, measuring 5,263 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,800 mm high, with a wheelbase of 3,130 mm.

In comparison, that’s bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and Kia EV9. It’s closer in size to the Li Auto L9.

Recent findings suggest that based on a 1,000V architecture with BYD’s Flash Charging tech, the electric SUV can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. For a full recharge, or to go from 10% to 97%, it takes just nine minutes.

After launching in China, BYD executive vice president Stella Li remarked the flagship SUV will go on sale in Europe and other overseas markets by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.
  • 23 announcement, the DOJ noted that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.
  • In a recent development, the recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.

As per a Nov. 23 announcement, the DOJ noted that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

In a recent development, the recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct. 29 in one of the biggest crypto heists ever.

Sources indicate that the DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

The assets are alleged to have been stolen from Binance and laundered by North Korean cybercriminals.

Significantly, the assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government earlier this month. With the fresh court filing, the potential recovery of the assets has taken another step forward.

The DOJ further claimed that U.S. authorities have successfully helped freeze, seize or return over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency since the attack in October.

This is nearly half of the total $6 billion-plus stolen from Binance, though the government did not provide details about how much of that has been returned to the exchange.

Sources indicate that the importance of collaboration between law enforcement agencies and crypto firms to ensure that hackers don't get away with stolen assets was stressed by Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

It has been revealed that “North Korean cyber hackers stole over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from Binance. But prompt coordination with both the government and our private sector partners helped to avoid the bulk of these assets from being lost,” Duva remarked.

U.S. authorities have further revealed the sophisticated money laundering techniques used by North Korean hackers to conceal their stolen cryptocurrency.

FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman stated that the regime uses intricate money laundering methods to convert stolen digital assets into funds for its illicit activities.

After the Binance hack, authorities rapidly worked to trace the stolen funds and coordinate with crypto service providers to block further transfers.

The U.S. Secret Service claimed that its investigators were able to detect and freeze some of the stolen funds within minutes of the hack.

Recent findings suggest that "The bad actors in this intrusion thought they could run from law enforcement. They've found out they were wrong," said Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cryptoslate ↗ Open Full Page

Robinhood Chain pays Ethereum 70% more than Base despite collecting 64% less in fees

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (477 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robinhood Chain paid Ethereum 70% more than Coinbase-backed Base to settle transactions, even though it collected 64% fewer user fees over 30 days.
  • The network spent approximately $25,700 on Ethereum settlement costs between Oct.
  • However, Base generated $2.97 million in transaction fees over the same period, nearly three times Robinhood Chain's $1.07 million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood Chain paid Ethereum 70% more than Coinbase-backed Base to settle transactions, even though it collected 64% fewer user fees over 30 days.

The network spent approximately $25,700 on Ethereum settlement costs between Oct. 23 and Nov. 21, compared with Base's $15,100, according to Castle Labs data compiled from growthepie.

However, Base generated $2.97 million in transaction fees over the same period, nearly three times Robinhood Chain's $1.07 million.

That disparity left Robinhood Chain spending $2.41 on Ethereum settlement for every $100 collected from people, compared with just 51 cents for Base.

The figures expose a significant difference in the networks' settlement costs, even as both retain the overwhelming majority of transaction fees after paying Ethereum.

The gap is particularly striking because Base consumed considerably more Ethereum data capacity.

In a recent development, according to Blobscan data, Base posted approximately 350,000 blobs during the period, nearly twice Robinhood Chain's 182,000. Blobs let Ethereum's layer-2 networks publish transaction data at lower cost.

Base consequently spent about $4,478 on blob fees, compared with Robinhood Chain's $2,315.

However, the remaining settlement costs tell a different story. Excluding blob fees, Robinhood Chain spent approximately $23,379, more than double Base's $10,602.

Those additional expenses include standard Ethereum transaction fees for posting data and updating settlement states.

Settlement and data-posting costs in USD. Labels show the UTC start dates of four seven-day periods in 2026. The article covers Nov. 20 and 21 separately.

Source: growthepie Robinhood Chain daily settlement fees · growthepie Base daily settlement fees.

The comparison highlights a broader imbalance in Ethereum's scaling economy, where layer-2 networks collect transaction fees while paying relatively little to the blockchain securing their operations.

Industry observers note that across all tracked Ethereum layer-2 networks, users paid approximately $5 million in fees during the 30 days ending Nov. 21, while the networks paid Ethereum just $74,500 for settlement and data availability.

That represents roughly 1.5% of user fees, leaving approximately 98.5% after Ethereum settlement expenses, before accounting for other operating and revenue-sharing costs.

Base and Robinhood Chain accounted for about $4.04 million of those combined fees but paid Ethereum only $40,800.

According to recent reports, the difference reflects how Ethereum's scaling architecture distributes economic activity. Layer-2 networks handle user transactions and collect their associated fees, while Ethereum provides settlement and data availability for a comparatively small charge.

For Ethereum, the resulting payments contribute to transaction fee burning and validator income, but remain modest relative to the economic activity taking place on its scaling networks.

The November figures raise two questions: whether Robinhood Chain can narrow its settlement-cost disadvantage against Base, and how much additional revenue Ethereum can capture as layer-2 networks continue handling most user activity.
